You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`, never run fmt in place on repo files; no internet), the repo layout/status, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `layout: schematic` (circuit schematics) — byte-identical to the original. Components `|component|` (IC body with `|pin|` children: side, number, labels like "EN/~SHDN" with overbar, `|space|` rail gaps, auto bilateral pin split, prefix/reference designators U1…), passive parts `|R|`, `|C|`, `|L|`, `|D|`, `|LED|`, `|Q|`, `|Y|`, `|F|`, `|FB|`, `|SW|`, `|BT|`, `|V|`, `|I|`, `|M|`, `|BZ|`, `|TP|`, `|J|` connectors (`pins: 4`, `rotate`), `|gnd|`, power flags (`|label| { symbol: power }` defines like `|vcc::label|`), net labels `|label|` (`shape: plain|round|…`), junction dots, `|nc|`, opamps, wires: `-` links that chain THROUGH 2-pin parts, net names from wire labels, one-ended label wires `j1.p1 -> "NSTDBY"`, plain-name runs `u1.en - "EN"`, wires merging at declared labels, warnings like `'u1' has no placed end — its chain falls back to the flow`, `cell:` placement on the schematic grid, sheet scaling (the schematic_hero sample scales the sheet: px per mm 5.5), `.lini-schematic` sheet wash, CSS rules (`.lini-sch-line`, `.lini-sch-solid`, `.lini-ref`, `.lini-junction`, `.lini-sch-tag-line`, …) and their order. IMPORTANT: the repo's desugar implementation already reproduces schematic lowering INCLUDING wire routing geometry for desugar output (src/desugar/schematic.rs, src/desugar/sch_geo.rs, 97–100% match on random schematics) — study and reuse it for the compile path rather than starting from zero. Put compile-side code in new module(s) (e.g. src/schematic.rs) with minimal hooks in scene.rs/layout.rs/render.rs/links.rs (schematic wires must not go through the general link router).

Test files: /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples prop_number, prop_pins, prop_prefix, prop_shape, skill_09, spec_46, spec_47 (error cases), blocks/skill_009; test_samples schematic.lini, schematic_parts.lini, schematic_blocks.lini, schematic_hero.lini. Write many synthetic schematics in /tmp/<you>/.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-sch/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini`; start: 171/246) and ensure nothing regresses; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on your branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace —
  fmt rewrites files in place. Copy inputs to /tmp/<you>/ first if you need in-place commands.
- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Status (after wave 2) — modules now in the tree
- `chart.rs` + `chart/*` (charts & pies, done), `table.rs` (tables/entity), `page.rs` (sheets,
  title-blocks), `sketch.rs` (draw: pen) + `drawing.rs` (stack/drawing layouts, holes, patterns,
  revolve/break/thread, planes, magnifier; see its notes on tagged segments, `drawing::ps`,
  `pattern_copy`), `icon.rs`/`image.rs` + `data/icons.txt`, `links.rs` + `route.rs` + `wires.rs`
  (link rendering + orthogonal router; `ctx.link_geo`), `desugar.rs` + `desugar/*` (complete; it
  contains its own lowering for tables, pages, trees/mindmaps, drawings, schematics incl. wire
  routing in `desugar/schematic.rs`/`sch_geo.rs` — reuse ideas from there), `format*` (fmt, done),
  `highlight.rs` (done).
- Pipeline (main.rs `compile_src`): parse → build_sheet → Builder (build_stmts, icon::validate,
  resolve_links, page::root_fixup, unworn_class_warnings) → Ctx → compute → drawing::expand
  (+recompute) → chart::validate → page::scale_units → drawing::prepare → image::check_sizes →
  layout::measure → drawing::size_warnings → links::compute → render → table::check_grids.
- Current asset pass rate: 146/209 (+25/37 in test_doc_examples/blocks). desugar/fmt/highlight
  are 246/246 on the corpus.

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE). test_doc_examples test_images test_samples 173 assets cards.lini chart_advanced.lini chart_hero.lini charts.lini desugar.lini drawing_annotations.lini drawing_gdt.lini drawing_section.lini drawing_sheet.lini drawing_turned.lini entity_hero.lini expr.lini floorplan.lini floorplan_parts.lini hello.lini hero.lini icons.lini layout.lini links.lini links_hard.lini links_medium.lini logo.lini mindmap.lini paint.lini palette.lini pcb.lini schematic.lini schematic_blocks.lini schematic_hero.lini schematic_parts.lini sequence.lini shapes.lini sketch.lini styles.lini templates.lini text_tables.lini tree.lini

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# show component box offsets for pin configurations
import sys, re
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

cfgs = sys.argv[1:]
for cfg in cfgs:
    # cfg like "L,L,R" sides
    pins = []
    for k, s in enumerate(cfg.split(',')):
        side = {'L': 'left', 'R': 'right', 'T': 'top', 'B': 'bottom', 'A': None, 'S': 'space'}[s]
        if side == 'space':
            pins.append('|space|')
        elif side:
            pins.append('|pin#p%d| { side: %s; }' % (k, side))
        else:
            pins.append('|pin#p%d|' % k)
    src = '|schematic| [ |component#d| "z" [ %s ] ]' % '; '.join(pins)
    o, e, c = run(src)
    m = re.search(r'data-id="d" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([-\d.]+)" height="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    sm = re.search(r'lini-schematic lini-block" transform="[^"]+">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([-\d.]+)" height="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    pinpos = re.findall(r'data-id="(p\d+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    print('%-12s comp@(%s,%s) rect y=%s h=%s  scope y=%s h=%s pins=%s %s' % (cfg, m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(4), m.group(6), sm.group(2), sm.group(4), [(p, y) for p, x, y in pinpos], e.strip()[:60]))

sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

cfgs = sys.argv[1:]
for cfg in cfgs:
    # cfg like "L,L,R" sides
    pins = []
    for k, s in enumerate(cfg.split(',')):
        side = {'L': 'left', 'R': 'right', 'T': 'top', 'B': 'bottom', 'A': None, 'S': 'space'}[s]
        if side == 'space':
            pins.append('|space|')
        elif side:
            pins.append('|pin#p%d| { side: %s; }' % (k, side))
        else:
            pins.append('|pin#p%d|' % k)
    src = '|schematic| [ |component#d| "z" [ %s ] ]' % '; '.join(pins)
    o, e, c = run(src)
    m = re.search(r'data-id="d" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([-\d.]+)" height="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    sm = re.search(r'lini-schematic lini-block" transform="[^"]+">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([-\d.]+)" height="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    pinpos = re.findall(r'data-id="(p\d+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    print('%-12s comp@(%s,%s) rect y=%s h=%s  scope y=%s h=%s pins=%s %s' % (cfg, m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(4), m.group(6), sm.group(2), sm.group(4), [(p, y) for p, x, y in pinpos], e.strip()[:60]))

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# lane offsets of chains from u1.c for various gaps
import sys, re
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

HEAD = '''{ layout: schematic; gap: %s; |vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ] }
|component#u1| "U" [ |pin#a| {side: left}; |pin#b| {side: left}; |pin#c| {side: right} ]
'''
def pos(svg, id_):
    m = re.search(r'data-id="%s" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)' % id_, svg)
    return (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2))) if m else None

def paths(svg):
    return re.findall(r'<path d="(M[^"]*)"/>\n    </g>', svg)

bodies = sys.argv[2:]
gaps = sys.argv[1].split(',')
for body in bodies:
    print('###', body)
    for g in gaps:
        src = HEAD % g + body.replace('\\n', '\n')
        o, e, c = run(src)
        u = pos(o, 'u1')
        ids = re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]+)" transform', o)
        tops = [i for i in ids if i not in ('a', 'b', 'c', 'u1', 'p1', 'p2', 'w', 'k')]
        rel = []
        for i in tops:
            p = pos(o, i)
            rel.append('%s(%g,%g)' % (i, p[0] - u[0], p[1] - u[1]))
        ls = re.findall(r'<g class="lini-link"[^>]*>\n\s*<path d="([^"]*)"', o)
        print('  gap %4s: %s | %s %s' % (g, ' '.join(rel), ' || '.join(ls), e.strip()[:80]))

from summ import run

part = sys.argv[1]  # e.g. R

|%s#r1| "1u"
u1.c - r1 - |gnd|''' % (gap, lab, part)

    print('%-12s tip=%8.4f lane=%g  lane-tip=%.4f' % (lab, tip - ux, rx - ux, rx - tip))

import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

body = sys.argv[1].replace('\\n', '\n')
labels = sys.argv[2:]
extra = os.environ.get('EXTRA', '')
for lab in labels:
    src = ('{ layout: schematic; %s |vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ] }\n' % extra) + \
        ('|component#u1| "U" [ |pin#a| {side: left}; |pin#b| {side: left}; |pin#c| "%s" {side: right} ]\n' % lab) + body
    o, e, c = run(src)
    u = re.search(r'data-id="u1" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    ux, uy = float(u.group(1)), float(u.group(2))
    ids = re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    rel = []
    for i, x, y in ids:
        if i in ('a', 'b', 'c', 'u1', 'p1', 'p2', 'w', 'k', 'plus', 'minus'):
            continue
        rel.append('%s(%g,%g)' % (i, float(x) - ux, float(y) - uy))
    ls = re.findall(r'<g class="lini-link"[^>]*>\n\s*<path d="([^"]*)"', o)
    tip = None
    m = re.search(r'<g class="lini-link"[^>]*>\n\s*<path d="M ([-\d.]+) ', o)
    if m: tip = float(m.group(1)) - ux
    print('%-10s tip=%8.4f %s | %s %s' % (lab, tip if tip is not None else 0, ' '.join(rel), ' || '.join(ls), e.strip()[:60]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fine scan: vary right-pin label; report (tip, satellite x offsets) sorted by tip, only where the result changes
import sys, re, os, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

body = sys.argv[1].replace('\\n', '\n')
target = sys.argv[2]  # id whose x offset we track
extra = os.environ.get('EXTRA', '')
chars = ['i', 'l', 'c', 'x', 'm', 'W']
labels = set()
for n in range(1, 4):
    for combo in itertools.product(chars, repeat=n):
        labels.add(''.join(combo))
rows = []
for lab in sorted(labels):
    src = ('{ layout: schematic; %s |vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ] }\n' % extra) + \
        ('|component#u1| "U" [ |pin#a| {side: left}; |pin#b| {side: left}; |pin#c| "%s" {side: right} ]\n' % lab) + body
    o, e, c = run(src)
    u = re.search(r'data-id="u1" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    ux = float(u.group(1))
    t = re.search(r'data-id="%s" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)' % target, o)
    m = re.search(r'<g class="lini-link"[^>]*>\n\s*<path d="M ([-\d.]+) ', o)
    tip = float(m.group(1)) - ux
    rows.append((tip, float(t.group(1)) - ux, lab))
rows.sort()
prev = None
for tip, x, lab in rows:
    if prev is None or x != prev[1]:
        if prev: print('   last tip %.4f -> %g' % (prev[0], prev[1]))
        print('tip %.4f -> %g (%s)' % (tip, x, lab))
    prev = (tip, x, lab)
print('   last tip %.4f -> %g' % (prev[0], prev[1]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# vary a satellite 2-pin component's width (via its value label); report its x offset from u1
import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

extra = os.environ.get('EXTRA', '')
labs = []
for n in range(1, 40):
    labs.append('i' * n)
for n in range(1, 14):
    labs.append('W' * n)
rows = []
for lab in labs:
    src = ('{ layout: schematic; %s }\n' % extra) + \
        '|component#u1| "U" [ |pin#a| {side: left}; |pin#b| {side: left}; |pin#c| {side: right} ]\n' + \
        ('|component#s| "%s" [ |pin#p| {side: top}; |pin#q| {side: bottom} ]\n' % lab) + \
        'u1.c - s.p\ns.q - |gnd|\n'
    o, e, c = run(src)
    u = re.search(r'data-id="u1" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)
    s = re.search(r'data-id="s" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="[-\d.]+" width="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    if not s:
        print(lab, 'no s', e[:100]); continue
    ux = float(u.group(1))
    sx = float(s.group(1)) - ux
    # extent of s: max of rect and value label
    m = re.search(r'data-id="s" transform[^\n]*\n(?:.*\n)*?\s*<g class="lini-node lini-part-value lini-block" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="[-\d.]+" width="([-\d.]+)"', o)
    vw = float(m.group(4)) if m else 0
    rw = float(s.group(4))
    rows.append((max(vw / 2, rw / 2 + 0.75), sx, lab))
rows.sort()
prev = None
for hw, x, lab in rows:
    if prev is None or x != prev[1]:
        if prev: print('   last hw %.4f -> %g' % (prev[0], prev[1]))
        print('hw %.4f -> %g (%s)' % (hw, x, lab))
    prev = (hw, x, lab)
print('   last hw %.4f -> %g' % (prev[0], prev[1]))

# compare the scope hull with the tight extent of all drawn items (incl. wires, labels)
import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

def tight(svg):
    # parse the scene: track transforms through <g> nesting; collect rect/line/path/ellipse boxes
    xs0, ys0, xs1, ys1 = [], [], [], []
    stack = [(0.0, 0.0)]
    lines = svg.split('\n')
    in_scene = False
    for l in lines:
        s = l.strip()
        if s.startswith('<g class="lini-scene">'):
            in_scene = True
            stack = [(0.0, 0.0)]
            continue
        if not in_scene:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# random small schematics for differential testing
import random, sys, os

PARTS = ['R', 'C', 'L', 'D', 'LED', 'F', 'Y', 'FB', 'SW', 'BT']
SIDES = ['left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom']

def gen(seed, level=1):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines = []
    root = rnd.random() < 0.8
    defs = ['|vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ]']
    if root:
        lines.append('{ layout: schematic; %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    else:
        lines.append('{ %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    body = []
    anchors = []
    na = rnd.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3]) if level >= 2 else rnd.choice([1, 2])
    pins_of = {}
    for k in range(na):
        aid = 'u%d' % (k + 1)
        kind = rnd.choice(['comp', 'comp', 'comp', 'J'])
        if kind == 'J':
            n = rnd.choice([3, 4, 5])
            extra = ''
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                extra = ' rotate: 180;'
            body.append('|J#%s| "CONN" { pins: %d;%s }' % (aid, n, extra))
            pins_of[aid] = [('p%d' % i, 'left' if '180' not in extra else 'right') for i in range(1, n + 1)]
        else:
            npins = rnd.choice([3, 4, 5, 6])
            ps = []
            used = set()
            for i in range(npins):
                side = rnd.choice(SIDES[:2] * 3 + SIDES[2:]) if level >= 2 else rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])
                pid = rnd.choice(['vin', 'vout', 'en', 'gnd', 'fb', 'sw', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'out', 'in'])
                while pid in used:
                    pid = pid + 'x'
                used.add(pid)
                num = ' number: %d;' % rnd.randint(1, 20) if rnd.random() < 0.5 else ''
                ps.append((pid, side, num))
            pins_of[aid] = [(p, s) for p, s, _ in ps]
            label = rnd.choice(['AMS1117', 'U', 'LM2596S-5.0', 'TPS'])
            pl = '; '.join('|pin#%s| { side: %s;%s }' % (p, s, n) for p, s, n in ps)
            body.append('|component#%s| "%s" [ %s ]' % (aid, label, pl))
        anchors.append(aid)
    sats = []
    nsat = rnd.randint(0, 3)
    for k in range(nsat):
        t = rnd.choice(PARTS)
        sid = '%s%d' % (t.lower(), k + 1)
        val = rnd.choice(['1k', '10u', '22u', '4k7', '100n', 'x'])
        body.append('|%s#%s| "%s"' % (t, sid, val))
        sats.append(sid)
    wires = []
    used_sats = set()
    for k in range(rnd.randint(1, 5)):
        a = rnd.choice(anchors)
        p, side = rnd.choice(pins_of[a])
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.2:
            wires.append('%s.%s - |gnd|' % (a, p))
        elif r < 0.35:
            wires.append('%s.%s - |vcc|' % (a, p))
        elif r < 0.5:
            wires.append('%s.%s - "%s"' % (a, p, rnd.choice(['EN', 'NSTDBY', 'TX', 'SDA_LINE'])))
        elif r < 0.55:
            wires.append('%s.%s -> "%s"' % (a, p, rnd.choice(['FLAG', 'OUT'])))
        elif r < 0.75 and sats:
            s = rnd.choice(sats)
            if s in used_sats:
                continue
            used_sats.add(s)
            end = rnd.choice(['|gnd|', '|vcc|', '"NET"', None])
            if end:
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s - %s' % (a, p, s, end))
            else:
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s' % (a, p, s))
        elif len(anchors) > 1:
            b = rnd.choice([x for x in anchors if x != a])
            q, _ = rnd.choice(pins_of[b])
            lab = ' "%s"' % rnd.choice(['3V3', 'VM']) if rnd.random() < 0.3 else ''
            wires.append('%s.%s - %s.%s%s' % (a, p, b, q, lab))
    if root:
        lines += body + wires
    else:
        lines.append('|schematic| [')
        lines += ['  ' + l for l in body + wires]
        lines.append(']')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    out = sys.argv[1]
    n = int(sys.argv[2])
    level = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 1
    base = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 0
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(n):
        open(os.path.join(out, 'g%04d.lini' % (base + i)), 'w').write(gen(base + i, level))

# vertical offset of a turned chain's first element from its pin row, for a
# configurable component and extra wires
import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

comp = sys.argv[1]   # e.g. "L,L,L,R"
chain = sys.argv[2]  # e.g. "u1.p0 - r1 - |gnd|"
extra = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else ''
pins = []
for k, s in enumerate(comp.split(',')):
    side = {'L': 'left', 'R': 'right', 'T': 'top', 'B': 'bottom', 'S': None}[s]
    pins.append('|space|' if side is None else '|pin#p%d| { side: %s; }' % (k, side))
src = '{ layout: schematic; |vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ] }\n|component#u1| "U" [ %s ]\n|component#u2| "V" [ |pin#a| { side: left; }; |pin#b| { side: left; }; |pin#c| { side: left; } ]\n|R#r1| "1k"\n%s\n%s\n' % (
    '; '.join(pins), chain.replace('\\n', '\n'), extra.replace('\\n', '\n'))
exes = ['/workspace/executable', '/tmp/bin-sch/executable'] if os.environ.get('BOTH') else ['/workspace/executable']
for exe in exes:
    o, e, c = run(src, exe=exe)
    pos = {i: (float(x), float(y)) for i, x, y in re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o)}
    u = pos.get('u1')
    out = []
    for i in ('r1', 'lini-cap-1', 'lini-cap-2'):
        if i in pos:
            out.append('%s(%g,%g)' % (i, pos[i][0] - u[0], pos[i][1] - u[1]))
    pins_y = []
    for k in range(len(comp.split(','))):
        pass
    print('%-14s %-22s %-20s %s %s' % (comp, chain, extra, ' '.join(out), e.strip()[:50]))

    new = set(ok)

    won = sorted(new - old)

# tiers of down chains: configurable component and chain statements; print element y offsets rel. u1
import sys, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/sch/scripts')
from summ import run

parts = '|R#r1| "1"\n|R#r2| "2"\n|R#r3| "3"\n|R#r4| "4"\n|C#c1| "c"\n'
src = '{ layout: schematic; |vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ] }\n|component#u1| "U" [ %s ]\n%s%s\n' % ('; '.join(pins), parts, body)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# for every rotated link label in original outputs: segment geometry, side chosen
import sys, re, os, subprocess
rows = []
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True).stdout
    for m in re.finditer(r'<path d="([^"]+)"/>\n\s*<text class="lini-link-label" x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)"[^>]*transform="rotate\(270', o):
        nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', m.group(1))]
        pts = list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))
        lx, ly = float(m.group(2)), float(m.group(3))
        # find the vertical segment holding the label
        for k in range(1, len(pts)):
            p, q = pts[k - 1], pts[k]
            if abs(p[0] - q[0]) < 1e-6 and min(p[1], q[1]) - 1e-6 <= ly <= max(p[1], q[1]) + 1e-6 and abs(abs(lx - p[0]) - 9.5) < 1e-6:
                side = 'R' if lx > p[0] else 'L'
                trav = 'D' if q[1] > p[1] else 'U'
                before = None
                after = None
                if k >= 2:
                    a = pts[k - 2]
                    before = 'R' if p[0] > a[0] else 'L'
                if k + 1 < len(pts):
                    c = pts[k + 1]
                    after = 'R' if c[0] > q[0] else 'L'
                rows.append((b, side, trav, before, after, k, len(pts) - 1))
                break
for r in rows:
    print('%-12s side %s travel %s before %s after %s seg %d/%d' % r)

# for wires ending at a vcc flag in original outputs: is a vertical approach drawn as a zero-jog Z?
import sys, re, os, subprocess, collections
stats = collections.Counter()
ex = {}
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True).stdout
    # vcc label ids
    vids = set(re.findall(r'class="lini-node lini-vcc[^"]*" data-id="([^"]+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o))
    vmap = {i: (float(x), float(y)) for i, x, y in vids}
    for m in re.finditer(r'data-from="([^"]+)" data-to="([^"]+)">\n\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o):
        fr, to, dd = m.groups()
        if to not in vmap and fr not in vmap:
            continue
        nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', dd)]
        pts = list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))
        kind = 'pin' if '.' in fr and fr.split('.')[-1] not in ('p1', 'p2', 'a', 'k', 'plus', 'minus') else 'station'
        n = len(pts)
        z = n == 4 and pts[1][0] == pts[2][0] and pts[1][1] == pts[2][1]
        key = (kind, n, z)
        stats[key] += 1
        ex.setdefault(key, (b, dd, vmap.get(to, vmap.get(fr))))
for k, v in stats.most_common():
    print(v, k, ex[k])

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (single message) asked me to join a reverse-engineering project: first read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely, then implement `layout: schematic` (circuit schematics) in our Rust reimplementation of the closed binary /workspace/executable ("lini 1.1.0", Lini source → SVG) so output is byte-identical: components with pins (side, number, labels like "EN/~SHDN", `|space|` gaps, auto bilateral split, prefixes/ref designators), passive parts (R, C, L, D, LED, Q, Y, F, FB, SW, BT, V, I, M, BZ, TP, J connectors with `pins:`/`rotate`), gnd, power flags (`|vcc::label| { symbol: power }`), net labels (shape plain/round/…), junction dots, `|nc|`, opamps, wires chaining through 2-pin parts, net names from wire labels, one-ended label wires, plain-name runs, wires merging at declared labels, warnings like "'u1' has no placed end — its chain falls back to the flow", `cell:` placement, sheet scaling, `.lini-schematic` wash, CSS rules and their order. IMPORTANT hint: reuse the repo's desugar lowering (src/desugar/schematic.rs, sch_geo.rs). Put compile-side code in new modules (e.g. src/schematic.rs) with minimal hooks in scene.rs/layout.rs/render.rs/links.rs; schematic wires must not go through the general link router. Test files: test_doc_examples prop_number, prop_pins, prop_prefix, prop_shape, skill_09, spec_46, spec_47 (error cases), blocks/skill_009; test_samples schematic.lini, schematic_parts.lini, schematic_blocks.lini, schematic_hero.lini. Write many synthetic schematics in /tmp/<you>/. Before committing run `python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-sch/executable /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_samples/*.lini /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini` (start 171/246), no regressions; keep `-a desugar`, `-a "fmt --stdout"`, `-a highlight` at 246/246. Commit on my branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits and gaps.

   Rules from ARCH.md/environment that must remain in effect (security/process constraints):
   - "Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output. NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes."
   - "No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust."
   - "Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary)."
   - "Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited."
   - "NEVER run `executable fmt FILE` (without --stdout) or our fmt on files inside /workspace — fmt rewrites files in place."
   - "Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP."
   - Worktree: /workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a3eceff6d2e2640b7; never bare `git stash`/`git stash pop`; git commit messages must end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" (note: my last two commits omitted this trailer — fix going forward).
   - Tool harness rejects complex bash (heredocs with `|`, loops with variables calling executables); write scripts with the Write tool into /tmp/sch/scripts and run them.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Original compile ≡ compile(desugar(src)) (verified on all schematic tests) → hybrid: run our desugar lowering (with origin spans) and substitute schematic scopes in the scene with lowered subtrees; lowered `.lini-*` classes form the chain (prim class last), pose classes `lini-pose-N`/`lini-mirror-x|y` are chain entries with no CSS.
   - Lattice: 20 px pin pitch; part centres/symbol attach points on lattice relative to scope centre; centering offset `round_lattice(-(mid))` (half away from zero); cell boundaries at odd multiples of 10 (`cell_half`), `snap_cells`.
   - Scope box = symmetric hull of anchors' exact drawn extents + satellites' reservations (+padding); root schematic viewBox = root box + padding, extended by wires/labels.
   - Grid pitch: `max(ceil20(gap), ceil20(right_k + 20 + left_{k+1}))` using cluster reaches; uncelled anchors fill row 1.
   - Component body shift: parity-padded columns/rows → rect & pinned labels offset (geo_off), rule: dy when no top/bottom pins, dx when no left/right pins.
   - Satellite seating: straight (element along pin facing): near edge ≥ ext+20, centre snapped; labels stack above (top pin of side)/below (bottom pin)/split; reservation includes labels. Turned (lane): first element clears own row and all wired pin rows beyond on same side by 20; tier-1 alignment of first elements across anchors in same grid row (U/D) and per anchor (L/R); min lane = snap(ext + 20 + near reservation) with part gap margin `10 + 20*floor(gap/40)`; base = max of side's minima; pin order up-chains (top first) then down-chains (bottom first); per pin parts first (declaration order, first fit from base), label-only chains start at outermost lane; conflicts: 2D reservation overlap, collinear runs, lane wire through boxes. Vertical part labels at x=24 flush-left (shift +w/2), mirrored to left when lane faces L.
   - Terms: pin stub tip, part station, symbol attach (gnd top, power bottom, nc left…), run far end with wire passing through (`through` = near end), flags attach by end facing wire.
   - Router: obstacles = geometric drawn boxes (component rect, stubs, value/ref, symbol paths, label boxes; not rows/columns/pin numbers) grown by CLEAR(10)+WIRE(1.5); landing out of own boxes; Dijkstra on lattice lines + obstacle edges, cost length + 20/bend; segment placement: staircase centred in channel snapped to nearest lattice line in channel (ties lower) else exact middle; detours hug first lattice line beyond obstacle or centre between obstacles. Runs: free port at near end, far end prefix.
   - Junction dots where ≥3 directions meet in a net; net names at `along` (0.5) of path, 9.5 above horizontal segments; vertical: right (+9.5, rotate 270) unless crowded (one-sided box margin 6 by own other segments/other wires) and left clear.
   - Errors: "'|type|' belongs in a 'layout: schematic'" (Y008 schematic-type, after compute), "'a - b' is already wired — a repeated wire means nothing on a sheet (previously at L:C)" (R022 duplicate-wire, JSON uses related span), warning Y007 schematic-seat.
   - Float artifact: vertical part→power-flag wires drawn as zero-jog Z ("M -40 -72 L -40 -86 L -40 -86 L -40 -100") in original for lanes -60..60 (abs), straight for |L|≥80; not yet reproduced.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/desugar/out.rs: added `pub origin: Option<crate::diag::Span>` to ONode (init None) and OLink.
   - src/desugar/lower.rs: `r.map(|mut o| { o.origin = Some(n.span); Item::Node(o) })` in Cx::node; sch_emit OLink `origin: Some(l.span)`, before/after generated nodes get `n.origin = Some(l.span)` when default; emit_link OLinks `origin: Some(p.span)`. tree.rs OLink `origin: None`.
   - src/desugar.rs: `desugar()` now calls `lower_all`; added `pub struct Lowered { sheet, items, used }`, `pub fn lower(src)`, re-exports `Item, OLink, ONode, SheetLine, LDecl`, `print_children`, `link_text`, `part_pins(ty, variant)`.
   - src/schematic.rs (new): module docs, `mod build; mod draw; mod net; mod place; mod router; mod seat; mod wire;`, CLASS_DEFAULTS (sch-line, sch-solid, sch-tag-line, pin-stub, pin-number, ref, part-value, tag-outline, tag-round, tag-flag-left/right/both, net-run, net-run-turned, sheet-caption), is_internal_class, PART_TYPES, FAMILY, State/STATE, take_onode, detect, prepare, root_scope, build_root, claims, shape_override, sheet_vars, check_scopes (dup wires first, then belongs-in).
   - src/schematic/build.rs, place.rs, net.rs (has a debug `eprintln!` in label_term under LINI_SCH_DBG printing label w/path.x/geo/o/pt — just added), seat.rs, router.rs, wire.rs (debug eprintln of ports/obstacles under LINI_SCH_DBG in route_one), draw.rs — as described in analysis.
   - Shared files: main.rs (mod schematic; prepare after build_sheet; build_root vs build_stmts; check_scopes after first compute; route after links::compute), scene.rs (claims hook; duplicate-id related span), layout.rs (schematic measure dispatch), links.rs (render_links insertion, extend_bbox hook), render.rs (internal class slots, SLOT_ORDER, shape_override hook, schematic root viewbox), style.rs (type_defaults adds CLASS_DEFAULTS), diag.rs (related field, Y007/Y008/R022, JSON related).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Bash harness rejected heredocs/loops with computed commands → use Write tool for scripts, run via python3/bash script files.
   - NaN rect broke sort in router → rebuild obstacle list without dropped entries (remap).
   - Pinned label positions ignored `translate` → set n.y = desired − comp.translate.1.
   - Staircase centering skipped first segment after simplify → bounds via landings instead of fixed_ends.
   - Cell-based obstacles vs raw: switched to geometric drawn boxes grown by 11.5; pin numbers/rows/columns excluded (fixed g1050 regression); restored skill_09 over-route.
   - Missing `--lini-label-ink` var → always declared with wires (root and nested).
   - Full comparison timed out at 2 min → use timeout 600000.
   - JSON duplicate errors needed `related` span → added to Diag.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved: lowering integration, no-wire layouts (track grid, cell grid, flow fallback, warnings), CSS order/vars, seated component bodies, flag outlines, wired seating (straight/lanes), routing basics, junctions, labels, errors. Corpus 179/246 (from 171), no regressions; desugar/fmt/highlight 246/246; JSON 215/246 (baseline 208). Generated sets: 341/500.
   - Ongoing/gaps: zero-jog Z float artifact; vertical label side edge cases (g1057); routing order/merging into existing nets (branching at trunk corners, g1079 hugging existing wire at −30); U-routes with fallback row (gap 160 chooses above); impossible/stray wires (g1074 "impossible (u1.bx -> u2.p1): fixed port blocked: a body covers the port's landing" + lini-stray drawing); bridges (R15/R16 tapped by FB), same-side pin ties (U at tip+10 with rotated label), run through points, clearance>20 error message, hero/blocks samples still failing; performance ~1.5 s on hero/blocks.

8. Current Work:
   Investigating why the original draws vertical part→power-flag wires as a zero-length-jog Z for lanes |L| ≤ 60 but straight for |L| ≥ 80. Survey (scripts/vccz2.py over gen1/gen2) showed Z lanes: −60, −40, −20, 0, 40, 60; straight lanes: −200..−80, 80..200. Was scanning schematic_hero output for similar Z patterns (none obvious in the listed wires).

9. Optional Next Step:

99	// a node's group origin from an ancestor's origin
100	pub fn origin_in(ctx: &Ctx, node: usize, anc: usize) -> (f64, f64) {
101	    let mut x = 0.0;
102	    let mut y = 0.0;
103	    let mut cur = node;
104	    while cur != anc {
105	        let n = &ctx.nodes[cur];
106	        let c = &ctx.comp[cur];
107	        x += n.x + c.translate.0 + n.geo_off.0;
108	        y += n.y + c.translate.1 + n.geo_off.1;
109	        match n.parent {
110	            Some(p) => cur = p,
111	            None => break,
112	        }
113	    }
114	    (x, y)
115	}

129	pub fn pose_of(ctx: &Ctx, i: usize) -> (u32, Option<char>) {
130	    let mut rot = 0;
131	    let mut mirror = None;
132	    for c in &ctx.nodes[i].chain {

143	// a vector under a pose: mirror first, then the clockwise turn
144	pub fn map_vec(dx: f64, dy: f64, rot: u32, mirror: Option<char>) -> (f64, f64) {
145	    let (mut dx, mut dy) = (dx, dy);
146	    match mirror {
147	        Some('x') => dy = -dy,
148	        Some('y') => dx = -dx,
149	        _ => {}
150	    }
151	    match rot {
152	        90 => (-dy, dx),
153	        180 => (-dx, -dy),
154	        270 => (dy, -dx),
155	        _ => (dx, dy),
156	    }
157	}

159	// a point of a w x h frame under a pose
160	pub fn map_pt(x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64, rot: u32, mirror: Option<char>) -> (f64, f64) {
161	    let (mut x, mut y) = (x, y);
162	    match mirror {
163	        Some('x') => y = h - y,
164	        Some('y') => x = w - x,
165	        _ => {}
166	    }
167	    match rot {
168	        90 => (h - y, x),
169	        180 => (w - x, h - y),
170	        270 => (y, w - x),
171	        _ => (x, y),
172	    }
173	}

192	// a label's connection point (label-local) and the way its wire leaves
193	fn label_term(ctx: &Ctx, l: usize) -> Option<(Kind, (f64, f64), Dir, Option<(f64, f64)>)> {
194	    let (rot, mirror) = pose_of(ctx, l);
195	    let n = &ctx.nodes[l];
196	    let w = n.w;
197	    if has(ctx, l, "net-run") || has(ctx, l, "net-run-turned") {
198	        // pose 0: the wire comes in from the right and runs to the left end
199	        let (fx, fy) = map_vec(-1.0, 0.0, rot, mirror);
200	        let len = if has(ctx, l, "net-run-turned") { n.h } else { w };
201	        let far = (fx * len / 2.0, fy * len / 2.0);
202	        let near = (-far.0, -far.1);
203	        let dir = Dir::of_vec(-fx, -fy);
204	        return Some((Kind::Run, far, dir, Some(near)));
205	    }
206	    // a tag attaches by whichever end faces its wire (resolved when seated
207	    // and routed): its two ends here
208	    if has(ctx, l, "tag-flag-right") || has(ctx, l, "tag-flag-left") || has(ctx, l, "tag-flag-both") || has(ctx, l, "tag-outline") {
209	        return Some((Kind::Flag, (-w / 2.0, 0.0), Dir::L, Some((w / 2.0, 0.0))));
210	    }
211	    let sym = prop_ident(ctx, l, "symbol")?;
212	    let (fw, fh, ax, ay) = symbol_attach(&sym)?;
213	    // the drawing node
214	    let path = n.children.iter().cloned().find(|&c| has(ctx, c, "sch-tag-line"))?;
215	    let (pw, ph) = if rot == 90 || rot == 270 { (fh, fw) } else { (fw, fh) };
216	    let (px, py) = map_pt(ax, ay, fw, fh, rot, mirror);
217	    let o = origin_in(ctx, path, l);
218	    // the drawing's frame sits at its group origin
219	    let _ = (pw, ph);
220	    let pt = (o.0 + px, o.1 + py);
221	    if std::env::var("LINI_SCH_DBG").is_ok() {
222	        eprintln!("label {} w {:?} path.x {:?} geo {:?} o {:?} pt {:?}", l, w, ctx.nodes[path].x, ctx.nodes[path].geo_off, o, pt);
223	    }
224	    // the wire leaves away from the drawing
225	    let (cx, cy) = (o.0 + pw / 2.0, o.1 + ph / 2.0);
226	    let dir = Dir::of_vec(pt.0 - cx, pt.1 - cy);
227	    Some((Kind::Symbol, pt, dir, None))
228	}

247	// a link end as a term
248	pub fn term(ctx: &Ctx, scope: usize, node: usize) -> Option<Term> {
249	    let dev = device_of(ctx, scope, node)?;
250	    if has(ctx, node, "pin") {
251	        // the stub's far end
252	        let stub = ctx.nodes[node].children.iter().cloned().find(|&c| has(ctx, c, "pin-stub"))?;
253	        let side = ctx.comp[stub].pin.clone().unwrap_or_default();
254	        let dir = Dir::of_side(side.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("left")).unwrap_or(Dir::L);
255	        let o = origin_in(ctx, stub, dev);
256	        let pts = match &ctx.nodes[stub].geo {
257	            Some(crate::scene::Geo::Points(p)) => p.clone(),
258	            _ => vec![(0.0, 0.0), (20.0, 0.0)],
259	        };
260	        let mut best = (o.0 + pts[0].0, o.1 + pts[0].1);
261	        let score = |p: (f64, f64)| -> f64 {
262	            let v = dir.vec();
263	            p.0 * v.0 + p.1 * v.1
264	        };
265	        for p in &pts {
266	            let q = (o.0 + p.0, o.1 + p.1);
267	            if score(q) > score(best) {
268	                best = q;
269	            }
270	        }
271	        return Some(Term { node, dev, kind: Kind::Pin, off: best, dir, through: None });
272	    }
273	    if node != dev && is_part(ctx, dev) && ctx.nodes[node].id.is_some() {
274	        let o = origin_in(ctx, node, dev);
275	        let dir = Dir::of_vec(o.0, o.1);
276	        return Some(Term { node, dev, kind: Kind::Station, off: o, dir, through: None });
277	    }
278	    if node == dev && is_label(ctx, node) {
279	        let (kind, off, dir, through) = label_term(ctx, node)?;
280	        return Some(Term { node, dev, kind, off, dir, through });
281	    }
282	    let _ = is_component;
283	    Some(Term { node, dev, kind: Kind::Other, off: (0.0, 0.0), dir: Dir::R, through: None })
284	}

286	// the wires of a scope, in statement order
287	pub fn wires(ctx: &Ctx, scope: usize) -> Vec<Wire> {
288	    let mut out = Vec::new();
289	    for (li, l) in ctx.links.iter().enumerate() {
290	        if l.container != scope {
291	            continue;
292	        }
293	        let (a, b) = match (term(ctx, scope, l.from), term(ctx, scope, l.to)) {
294	            (Some(a), Some(b)) => (a, b),
295	            _ => continue,
296	        };
297	        out.push(Wire { li, a, b, span: l.span });
298	    }
299	    out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# for wires ending at a vcc flag in original outputs: is a vertical approach drawn as a zero-jog Z?
import sys, re, os, subprocess, collections
stats = collections.Counter()
ex = {}
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True).stdout
    # vcc label ids
    vids = set(re.findall(r'class="lini-node lini-vcc[^"]*" data-id="([^"]+)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o))
    vmap = {i: (float(x), float(y)) for i, x, y in vids}
    for m in re.finditer(r'data-from="([^"]+)" data-to="([^"]+)">\n\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o):
        fr, to, dd = m.groups()
        if to not in vmap and fr not in vmap:
            continue
        nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', dd)]
        pts = list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))
        kind = 'pin' if '.' in fr and fr.split('.')[-1] not in ('p1', 'p2', 'a', 'k', 'plus', 'minus') else 'station'
        n = len(pts)
        z = n == 4 and pts[1][0] == pts[2][0] and pts[1][1] == pts[2][1]
        key = (kind, n, z)
        stats[key] += 1
        ex.setdefault(key, (b, dd, vmap.get(to, vmap.get(fr))))
for k, v in stats.most_common():
    print(v, k, ex[k])

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. #!/usr/bin/env python3
# summarize an SVG from lini: viewBox, nodes at depth (indent based), links
import sys, re, subprocess, os, tempfile

def run(src, args=None, exe='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='summ', dir='/tmp/sch')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + (args or []) + ['in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode

def summarize(svg, depth=1, show_rect=False):
    out = []
    m = re.search(r'viewBox="([^"]+)"', svg)
    if m: out.append('viewBox ' + m.group(1))
    lines = svg.split('\n')
    in_links = False
    base = None
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if '<g class="lini-scene">' in l:
            base = len(l) - len(l.lstrip()) + 2
            continue
        if '<g class="lini-links"' in l:
            in_links = True
            continue
        if in_links:
            s = l.strip()
            if s.startswith('<g class="lini-link"'):
                out.append('LINK ' + re.sub(r'<g class="lini-link" ', '', s).rstrip('>'))
            elif s.startswith('<path'):
                out.append('   ' + s)
            elif s.startswith('<text'):
                out.append('   ' + s)
            elif 'lini-junction' in s:
                out.append('JUNC ' + re.search(r'transform="([^"]+)"', s).group(1))
            continue
        if base is None: continue
        ind = len(l) - len(l.lstrip())
        s = l.strip()
        if s.startswith('<g class="lini-node'):
            lvl = (ind - base) // 2
            if lvl < depth:
                cls = re.search(r'class="([^"]+)"', s).group(1).replace('lini-node ', '').replace('lini-', '')
                did = re.search(r'data-id="([^"]+)"', s)
                tr = re.search(r'transform="([^"]+)"', s).group(1)
                txt = ''
                # next line rect
                nxt = lines[i + 1].strip() if i + 1 < len(lines) else ''
                rect = ''
                if show_rect and nxt.startswith('<rect'):
                    rect = ' ' + re.sub(r' rx="[^"]*" ry="[^"]*"', '', nxt)
                out.append('  ' * lvl + '%s%s %s%s' % (cls, ('#' + did.group(1)) if did else '', tr, rect))
    return '\n'.join(out)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    depth = 1
    rect = False
    exe = '/workspace/executable'
    while args and args[0].startswith('-'):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# summarize an SVG from lini: viewBox, nodes at depth (indent based), links
import sys, re, subprocess, os, tempfile

def run(src, args=None, exe='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='summ', dir='/tmp/sch')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe] + (args or []) + ['in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode

def summarize(svg, depth=1, show_rect=False):
    out = []
    m = re.search(r'viewBox="([^"]+)"', svg)
    if m: out.append('viewBox ' + m.group(1))
    lines = svg.split('\n')
    in_links = False
    base = None
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if '<g class="lini-scene">' in l:
            base = len(l) - len(l.lstrip()) + 2
            continue
        if '<g class="lini-links"' in l:
            in_links = True
            continue
        if in_links:
            s = l.strip()
            if s.startswith('<g class="lini-link"'):
                out.append('LINK ' + re.sub(r'<g class="lini-link" ', '', s).rstrip('>'))
            elif s.startswith('<path'):
                out.append('   ' + s)
            elif s.startswith('<text'):
                out.append('   ' + s)
            elif 'lini-junction' in s:
                out.append('JUNC ' + re.search(r'transform="([^"]+)"', s).group(1))
            continue
        if base is None: continue
        ind = len(l) - len(l.lstrip())
        s = l.strip()
        if s.startswith('<g class="lini-node'):
            lvl = (ind - base) // 2
            if lvl < depth:
                cls = re.search(r'class="([^"]+)"', s).group(1).replace('lini-node ', '').replace('lini-', '')
                did = re.search(r'data-id="([^"]+)"', s)
                tr = re.search(r'transform="([^"]+)"', s).group(1)
                txt = ''
                # next line rect
                nxt = lines[i + 1].strip() if i + 1 < len(lines) else ''
                rect = ''
                if show_rect and nxt.startswith('<rect'):
                    rect = ' ' + re.sub(r' rx="[^"]*" ry="[^"]*"', '', nxt)
                out.append('  ' * lvl + '%s%s %s%s' % (cls, ('#' + did.group(1)) if did else '', tr, rect))
    return '\n'.join(out)

if __name__ == '__main__':

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# vs.py BIN_A BIN_B files... : which files pass with A but not B and vice versa
import sys, os, subprocess
A, B = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sys.argv[3:]
def passes(exe, f, orig_cache={}):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    if f not in orig_cache:
        orig_cache[f] = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r1 = orig_cache[f]
    try:
        r2 = subprocess.run([exe, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False
    return r1.stdout == r2.stdout and r1.stderr == r2.stderr and r1.returncode == r2.returncode
onlyA, onlyB, both = [], [], 0
for f in files:
    a = passes(A, f); b = passes(B, f)
    if a and not b: onlyA.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if b and not a: onlyB.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if a and b: both += 1
print('both %d, only A %d, only B %d' % (both, len(onlyA), len(onlyB)))
print('only A:', ' '.join(onlyA))
print('only B:', ' '.join(onlyB))

# mk.py [--scope 'props'] DIR NAME 'body lines separated by ;;' : write a schematic test file with the standard stylesheet

d, name, body = args[0], args[1], args[2]

  |s::group| { layout: schematic; }

}
