#!/usr/bin/env python3
# where does a tag above a lone top pin switch from an end to its bottom edge?
import subprocess, os, re, sys
d = '/tmp/sch/t4'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
shape = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'right'
for n in range(1, 16):
    t = 'N' * n
    src = '''{
  |s::group| { layout: schematic; }
}
|s| [
  |component#U1| [ |pin#A| { side: top; }; |pin#B| { side: bottom; }; |pin#Z| { side: right; } ]
  |label#na| "%s" { shape: %s; }
  U1.A - na
]
''' % (t, shape)
    p = os.path.join(d, 'ts.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'ts.lini'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    m = re.search(r'data-id="na" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="[-\d.]+" width="([\d.]+)"', o)
    path = re.search(r'data-to="na">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o).group(1)
    r = re.search(r'lini-s lini-group[^\n]*\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)"', o).group(1)
    print(n, m.group(1), m.group(4), 'rect', r, path)

import subprocess, os, re, sys
d = '/tmp/sch/t4'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
shape = 'right'
extra = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ''
for n in range(1, 12):
    t = 'N' * n
    src = '''{
  |s::group| { layout: schematic; }
}
|s| [
  |component#U1| [ |pin#A| { side: top; }; |pin#B| { side: bottom; }; |pin#Z| { side: right; } ]
  %s
  |label#na| "%s" { shape: %s; }
  U1.A - na
]
''' % (extra, t, shape)
    p = os.path.join(d, 'ts.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'ts.lini'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    m = re.search(r'data-id="na" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="[-\d.]+" width="([\d.]+)"', o)
    path = re.search(r'data-to="na">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o).group(1)
    r = re.search(r'lini-s lini-group[^\n]*\n\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)"', o).group(1)
    u = re.search(r'data-id="U1" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', o).groups()
    print(n, 'tag', m.group(1), m.group(2), 'w', m.group(4), 'rect', r, 'U1', u, path)

import sys, os, subprocess, hashlib
spec = sys.argv[1]
env = dict(os.environ)
for kv in spec.split(';'):
    if '=' in kv:
        k, v = kv.split('=', 1)
        env[k] = v
cache = '/tmp/sch/origcache'
os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
ok = 0; fails = []
for f in sys.argv[2:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    src = open(f, 'rb').read()
    h = hashlib.sha1(src + f.encode()).hexdigest()
    cp = os.path.join(cache, h)
    if os.path.exists(cp + '.out'):
        o1 = open(cp + '.out', 'rb').read(); e1 = open(cp + '.err', 'rb').read()
    else:
        r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
        o1, e1 = r1.stdout, r1.stderr
        open(cp + '.out', 'wb').write(o1); open(cp + '.err', 'wb').write(e1)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-sch/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=env)
    if o1 == r2.stdout and e1 == r2.stderr:
        ok += 1
    else:
        fails.append(b)
print(spec, ok, len(sys.argv) - 2)
if os.environ.get('SHOWFAIL'):
    print(' '.join(fails))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# vs2.py BIN_A BIN_B files... : which files pass with A but not B and vice versa (original cached)
import sys, os, subprocess, hashlib
A, B = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sys.argv[3:]
cache = '/tmp/sch/origcache'
os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
def orig(f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    src = open(f, 'rb').read()
    h = hashlib.sha1(src + f.encode()).hexdigest()
    cp = os.path.join(cache, h)
    if os.path.exists(cp + '.out'):
        return open(cp + '.out', 'rb').read(), open(cp + '.err', 'rb').read()
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    open(cp + '.out', 'wb').write(r1.stdout); open(cp + '.err', 'wb').write(r1.stderr)
    return r1.stdout, r1.stderr
def passes(exe, f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o1, e1 = orig(f)
    try:
        r2 = subprocess.run([exe, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=60)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False
    return o1 == r2.stdout and e1 == r2.stderr
onlyA, onlyB, both = [], [], 0
for f in files:
    a = passes(A, f); b = passes(B, f)
    if a and not b: onlyA.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if b and not a: onlyB.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if a and b: both += 1
print('both %d, only A %d, only B %d (of %d)' % (both, len(onlyA), len(onlyB), len(files)))
print('only A:', ' '.join(onlyA))
print('only B:', ' '.join(onlyB))

# vs2.py BIN_A BIN_B files... : which files pass with A but not B and vice versa (original cached)
import sys, os, subprocess, hashlib
A, B = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sys.argv[3:]
cache = '/tmp/sch/origcache'
os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
def orig(f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    src = open(f, 'rb').read()
    h = hashlib.sha1(src + f.encode()).hexdigest()
    cp = os.path.join(cache, h)
    if os.path.exists(cp + '.out'):
        return open(cp + '.out', 'rb').read(), open(cp + '.err', 'rb').read()
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    open(cp + '.out', 'wb').write(r1.stdout); open(cp + '.err', 'wb').write(r1.stderr)
    return r1.stdout, r1.stderr
def passes(exe, f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o1, e1 = orig(f)
    try:
        r2 = subprocess.run([exe, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=60)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False
    return o1 == r2.stdout and e1 == r2.stderr
onlyA, onlyB, both = [], [], 0
for f in files:
    a = passes(A, f); b = passes(B, f)
    if a and not b: onlyA.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if b and not a: onlyB.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if a and b: both += 1
print('both %d, only A %d, only B %d (of %d)' % (both, len(onlyA), len(onlyB), len(files)))
print('only A:', ' '.join(onlyA))
print('only B:', ' '.join(onlyB))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# originals whose net name is not at the path's midpoint (single-label wires)
import re, os, subprocess, glob
files = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/sch/gen1/*.lini') + glob.glob('/tmp/sch/gen2/*.lini'))
for f in files:
    d = os.path.dirname(f); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    for m in re.finditer(r'<path d="([^"]+)"/>\s*<text class="lini-link-label" x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)"([^>]*)>([^<]*)</text>\s*</g>', o):
        nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', m.group(1))]
        pts = list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))
        lx, ly = float(m.group(2)), float(m.group(3))
        rot = 'rotate' in m.group(4)
        total = sum(abs(pts[k][0] - pts[k-1][0]) + abs(pts[k][1] - pts[k-1][1]) for k in range(1, len(pts)))
        s = total / 2
        for k in range(1, len(pts)):
            p, q = pts[k-1], pts[k]
            L = abs(q[0] - p[0]) + abs(q[1] - p[1])
            if s <= L + 1e-9 or k == len(pts) - 1:
                fr = s / L if L else 0
                x = p[0] + (q[0] - p[0]) * fr; y = p[1] + (q[1] - p[1]) * fr
                break
            s -= L
        if rot:
            ok = abs(ly - y) < 0.01
        else:
            ok = abs(lx - x) < 0.01
        if not ok:
            print(b, m.group(5), 'label', lx, ly, 'mid', round(x, 4), round(y, 4), m.group(1))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# random small schematics for differential testing
import random, sys, os

PARTS = ['R', 'C', 'L', 'D', 'LED', 'F', 'Y', 'FB', 'SW', 'BT']
SIDES = ['left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom']

def gen(seed, level=1):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines = []
    root = rnd.random() < 0.8
    defs = ['|vcc::label| { symbol: power } [ "5V" ]']
    if root:
        lines.append('{ layout: schematic; %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    else:
        lines.append('{ %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    body = []
    anchors = []
    na = rnd.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3]) if level >= 2 else rnd.choice([1, 2])
    pins_of = {}
    for k in range(na):
        aid = 'u%d' % (k + 1)
        kind = rnd.choice(['comp', 'comp', 'comp', 'J'])
        if kind == 'J':
            n = rnd.choice([3, 4, 5])
            extra = ''
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                extra = ' rotate: 180;'
            body.append('|J#%s| "CONN" { pins: %d;%s }' % (aid, n, extra))
            pins_of[aid] = [('p%d' % i, 'left' if '180' not in extra else 'right') for i in range(1, n + 1)]
        else:
            npins = rnd.choice([3, 4, 5, 6])
            ps = []
            used = set()
            for i in range(npins):
                side = rnd.choice(SIDES[:2] * 3 + SIDES[2:]) if level >= 2 else rnd.choice(['left', 'right'])
                pid = rnd.choice(['vin', 'vout', 'en', 'gnd', 'fb', 'sw', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'out', 'in'])
                while pid in used:
                    pid = pid + 'x'
                used.add(pid)
                num = ' number: %d;' % rnd.randint(1, 20) if rnd.random() < 0.5 else ''
                ps.append((pid, side, num))
            pins_of[aid] = [(p, s) for p, s, _ in ps]
            label = rnd.choice(['AMS1117', 'U', 'LM2596S-5.0', 'TPS'])
            pl = '; '.join('|pin#%s| { side: %s;%s }' % (p, s, n) for p, s, n in ps)
            body.append('|component#%s| "%s" [ %s ]' % (aid, label, pl))
        anchors.append(aid)
    sats = []
    nsat = rnd.randint(0, 3)
    for k in range(nsat):
        t = rnd.choice(PARTS)
        sid = '%s%d' % (t.lower(), k + 1)
        val = rnd.choice(['1k', '10u', '22u', '4k7', '100n', 'x'])
        body.append('|%s#%s| "%s"' % (t, sid, val))
        sats.append(sid)
    wires = []

for f in files:

    for m in re.finditer(r'<path d="([^"]+)"/>\s*<text class="lini-link-label" x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)"[^>]*rotate\(270[^>]*>([^<]*)<', o):

        for k in range(1, len(pts)):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# vside.py FILE: for each upright net name in the original, which wire segments crowd either side
import re, sys, os, subprocess
f = sys.argv[1]
m_ = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 6.0
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
wires = []
for m in re.finditer(r'data-from="([^"]+)" data-to="([^"]+)">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o):
    nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', m.group(3))]
    wires.append((m.group(1) + '->' + m.group(2), list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))))
# node boxes (approx: translate + first rect)
nodes = []
for m in re.finditer(r'<g class="lini-node ([^"]*)"(?: data-id="([^"]*)")? transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">\s*<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([\d.]+)" height="([\d.]+)"', o):
    pass
for m in re.finditer(r'<path d="([^"]+)"/>\s*<text class="lini-link-label" x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)"[^>]*rotate\(270[^>]*>([^<]*)<', o):
    nums = [float(v) for v in re.findall(r'-?[\d.]+', m.group(1))]
    pts = list(zip(nums[0::2], nums[1::2]))
    lx, ly = float(m.group(2)), float(m.group(3))
    text = m.group(4)
    # find the trace x
    for k in range(1, len(pts)):
        (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = pts[k - 1], pts[k]
        if abs(x0 - x1) < 1e-6 and min(y0, y1) - 1e-6 <= ly <= max(y0, y1) + 1e-6 and abs(abs(lx - x0) - 9.5) < 1e-3:
            x = x0
            break
    tw = 7.0 * len(text)  # rough
    print('label', text, 'at', lx, ly, 'trace x', x, 'side', 'R' if lx > x else 'L')
    for side in (1, -1):
        bx = [x, ly - tw / 2 - m_, x + 9.5 + 5.5 + m_, ly + tw / 2 + m_] if side > 0 else [x - 9.5 - 5.5 - m_, ly - tw / 2 - m_, x, ly + tw / 2 + m_]
        hits = []
        for name, ps in wires:
            for j in range(1, len(ps)):
                a, c = ps[j - 1], ps[j]
                x_0, x_1 = min(a[0], c[0]), max(a[0], c[0])
                y_0, y_1 = min(a[1], c[1]), max(a[1], c[1])
                if x_0 < bx[2] and x_1 > bx[0] and y_0 < bx[3] and y_1 > bx[1] or (x_0 == x_1 and bx[0] < x_0 < bx[2] and y_0 < bx[3] and y_1 > bx[1]) or (y_0 == y_1 and bx[1] < y_0 < bx[3] and x_0 < bx[2] and x_1 > bx[0]):
                    hits.append((name, a, c))
        print('  side', 'R' if side > 0 else 'L', 'box', [round(v, 1) for v in bx], 'hits', hits)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# realistic small schematics: ICs with sided pins, decoupling, pull-ups, dividers, LEDs, runs,
# tags, power flags, bridges and straight ties between neighbouring ICs
import random, sys, os

def gen(seed):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    root = rnd.random() < 0.7
    defs = ['|v5::label| { symbol: power; } [ "5V" ]', '|v3::label| { symbol: power; } [ "3V3" ]']
    lines = []
    if root:
        lines.append('{ layout: schematic; %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    else:
        lines.append('{ %s }' % ' '.join(defs))
    body, wires = [], []
    n_ic = rnd.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3])
    ics = []
    use_cells = n_ic > 1 and rnd.random() < 0.6
    for k in range(n_ic):
        uid = 'U%d' % (k + 1)
        left = rnd.sample(['VIN', 'EN', 'IN', 'SDA', 'SCL', 'RX', 'TX', 'RST'], rnd.randint(1, 4))
        right = rnd.sample(['OUT', 'FB', 'SW', 'PG', 'MISO', 'MOSI', 'CLK', 'NC1'], rnd.randint(1, 4))
        bottom = ['GND'] if rnd.random() < 0.6 else []
        top = ['VCC'] if rnd.random() < 0.3 else []
        pins = [(p, 'left') for p in left] + [(p, 'right') for p in right] + [(p, 'bottom') for p in bottom] + [(p, 'top') for p in top]
        rnd.shuffle(pins) if rnd.random() < 0.2 else None
        cell = ' { cell: %d 1; }' % (k + 1) if use_cells else ''
        pl = '\n'.join('    |pin#%s| { side: %s;%s }' % (p, s, ' number: %d;' % rnd.randint(1, 16) if rnd.random() < 0.5 else '') for p, s in pins)
        body.append('|component#%s| "%s"%s [\n%s\n  ]' % (uid, rnd.choice(['LM317', 'TPS5430', 'ATtiny85', 'MCP2551', 'NE555', 'AMS1117']), cell, pl))
        ics.append((uid, pins))
    nparts = 0
    def part(t, val):
        nonlocal nparts
        nparts += 1
        pid = '%s%d' % ({'R': 'R', 'C': 'C', 'L': 'L', 'D': 'D', 'LED': 'D'}[t], nparts)
        body.append('|%s#%s| "%s"' % (t, pid, val))
        return pid
    for uid, pins in ics:
        for p, s in pins:
            r = rnd.random()
            if p == 'GND':
                wires.append('%s.%s - |gnd|' % (uid, p))
            elif p in ('VIN', 'VCC'):
                fl = rnd.choice(['|v5|', '|v3|'])
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s' % (uid, p, fl))
                if rnd.random() < 0.7:
                    c = part('C', rnd.choice(['100n', '10u', '1u']))
                    wires.append('%s.%s - %s - |gnd|' % (uid, p, c))
            elif r < 0.25:
                wires.append('%s.%s - "%s"' % (uid, p, p + rnd.choice(['', '_A', '_LINE'])))
            elif r < 0.35:
                wires.append('%s.%s -> "%s"' % (uid, p, p + '_OUT'))
            elif r < 0.5:
                rr = part('R', rnd.choice(['10k', '4k7', '100k']))
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s - %s' % (uid, p, rr, rnd.choice(['|v3|', '|v5|', '|gnd|'])))
            elif r < 0.6:
                rr = part('R', '1k')
                led = part('LED', rnd.choice(['red', 'green']))
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s - %s - |gnd|' % (uid, p, rr, led))
            elif r < 0.68:
                c = part('C', rnd.choice(['100n', '22u']))
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s - |gnd|' % (uid, p, c))
            elif r < 0.72:
                wires.append('%s.%s - |nc|' % (uid, p))
    # ties and bridges between neighbouring ICs
    for k in range(len(ics) - 1):
        a, b = ics[k], ics[k + 1]
        ra = [p for p, s in a[1] if s == 'right']
        lb = [p for p, s in b[1] if s == 'left']
        if ra and lb and rnd.random() < 0.7:
            pa, pb = rnd.choice(ra), rnd.choice(lb)
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s.%s%s' % (a[0], pa, b[0], pb, ' "%s"' % rnd.choice(['VBUS', 'NET1']) if rnd.random() < 0.3 else ''))
            else:
                l = part(rnd.choice(['R', 'L']), rnd.choice(['10u', '33R']))
                wires.append('%s.%s - %s - %s.%s' % (a[0], pa, l, b[0], pb))
    if root:
        lines += body + wires
    else:
        lines.append('|sheet::group| { layout: schematic; padding: 20; }')
        lines = [lines[0][:-1] + ' |sheet::group| { layout: schematic; } }']
        lines.append('|sheet| [')
        lines += ['  ' + l.replace('\n', '\n  ') for l in body + wires]
        lines.append(']')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    out = sys.argv[1]
    n = int(sys.argv[2])
    base = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(n):
        open(os.path.join(out, 'r%04d.lini' % (base + i)), 'w').write(gen(base + i))

import sys, os, subprocess, re
f, target = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
src = open(f).read().split('\n')
d = '/tmp/sch/abl'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
def path_of(text):
    p = os.path.join(d, 'a.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(text)

    m = re.search(r'data-from="%s" data-to="%s">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"' % tuple(target.split('->')), o)

print('full:', path_of('\n'.join(src)))
for i, l in enumerate(src):

    if ' - ' in s and not s.startswith('|') and s != target.replace('->', ' - '):

# bridge tail vs gap
cd /tmp/sch
A='|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#X| { side: left; }; |pin#A| { side: right; }; |pin#Y| { side: right; } ]'
B='|component#U2| { cell: 2 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: left; }; |pin#B| { side: left; }; |pin#Q| { side: left; }; |pin#Z| { side: right; } ]'
for g in 40 60 100 140 200; do
  python3 scripts/mk.py --scope "gap: $g;" t10 bt "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.B - C2 - |gnd|"
  o=$(python3 scripts/summ.py -d 2 t10/bt.lini | grep -E "block#(U1|U2|R1|C[0-9])" | sed 's/.*block#//' | tr '\n' ' ')

  echo "gap $g"; echo "   O $o"; echo "   M $m"
done

#!/bin/bash
# bridge tail vs the far anchor's lanes
cd /tmp/sch
A='|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#X| { side: left; }; |pin#A| { side: right; }; |pin#Y| { side: right; } ]'
B='|component#U2| { cell: 2 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: left; }; |pin#B| { side: left; }; |pin#Q| { side: left; }; |pin#Z| { side: right; } ]'
run() {
  python3 scripts/mk.py t10 bt "$1"
  o=$(python3 scripts/summ.py -d 2 t10/bt.lini | grep -E "block#(U1|U2|R1|C[0-9])" | sed 's/.*block#//' | tr '\n' ' ')
  m=$(python3 scripts/summ.py -m -d 2 t10/bt.lini | grep -E "block#(U1|U2|R1|C[0-9])" | sed 's/.*block#//' | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$2"; echo "   O $o"; echo "   M $m"
}
run "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B" "plain"
run "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.B - C2 - |gnd|" "B has a lane"
run "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.P - C2 - |gnd|" "P (above) has a down lane"
run "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.Q - C2 - |gnd|" "Q (below) has a down lane"
run "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;|C#C3| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.P - C2 - |gnd|;;U2.B - C3 - |gnd|" "P and B lanes"

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists the agents and Claude sessions this session can see — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions, each row labeled by kind — plus this session's own name, the one other sessions use to message it. This session has no SendMessage tool, so it cannot message them with it; other sessions can still message this one. To reply, use your host application's own messaging tool if it provides one — otherwise a reply from here is not possible, and if one is needed, tell your user.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

1. Primary Request and Intent:

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Original compile ≡ compile(desugar(src)); hybrid: our desugar lowering substitutes schematic scopes; lowered `.lini-*` classes; pose classes `lini-pose-N`/`lini-mirror-x|y`.
   - 20 px lattice; gap margin m = 10 + 20*floor(gap/40); cell_half; scope box = symmetric hull of anchors' extents + satellites' reservations.
   - Straight elements: aligned per side to deepest (U/D across anchors of a grid row; L/R across anchors of a grid column; nc symbols exempt); displaced (+y for rows, +x for columns, a pitch at a time) when cells overlap cells or keep overlaps keep (vertical parts in top/bottom rows keep x±m; labels keep their rect cells; text not included); parts seated before labels, in part declaration order; displaced row part reads labels below (stack +1); hull uses union(cells, keep). Straight chains on a pin that also turns lanes on that side are deferred and placed a pitch past those lanes' cells (and lanes crossing their row).
   - Lanes: pins whose chains ALL run toward the low end first (low end first), others from the far end; parts first in declaration order; label-only chains start at the outermost lane of the pin's *parts* (else base); tapped bridges (a chain whose walk reaches another hop's first part) clear only their own row and don't align; walks stop at claimed devices (other hops' first parts).
   - Grid: anchor_cells (uncelled anchors fill row 1); direct pin-to-pin wires between adjacent anchors (same row/col) add a pitch each to the gap: need = ceil(right + left + 20*max(1,n)); first facing wire aligns pins (anchor whose pin coordinate is lower shifts by the difference); bridges between facing adjacent anchors placed in the gap: first part at ceil(near_a + 20 + m) from first anchor, later parts walk (+pitch), far anchor at ceil(max(gap, m + near_b)) past last part.
   - Router: obstacles = drawn boxes grown by CLEAR(10) + the box's stroke width (stubs/paths 11.5, text/unstroked 10, refs +1.5 vertically, tag outlines = label box inset by sw/2 grown 11.5; parts' top box not an obstacle); horizontal station ports: own body grown by CLEAR only, detour off them keeps landing; place() uses place_obs (full clearance) and boxes straddling a segment bound the channel on their side; free (run) ports: landing = port, own boxes kept, segments collinear with the port pass own boxes; same-net runs never block; heap ordering quantized to 1e-6; bend cost 2*CLEAR; ties on one side drawn as U at farthest tip + CLEAR; hair-out-of-line ports (|Δ|<1e-6) drawn as zero-jog step at landing midpoint (reproduces float artifact); satellites placed as (x + s.x) + ox (lattice coords then centred) to match original float arithmetic.
   - Runs: joined at first lattice line in from near end; first wire travels its length; later wires choose back (free port) vs onward from far end (cheaper path_cost = length + 20/bend). Turned runs: w = text h + pad, h = max(height, text w + pads), text at ±(w/2+gap) rotated 270 (side L when lane faces L).
   - Nudging: segments of different nets on one line (overlapping or touching) spread CLEAR apart centred on the line, ordered by pairwise turn constraints; port-adjacent groups skipped.
   - Net names: multiple per wire with `along` list; upright side = side of previous horizontal travel unless crowded (margin 6, own other segments + other wires), both crowded → right; slide ±4 steps (back first) when overlapping previous wires' names or label nodes (wire's own end devices excluded; same-wire labels don't block).
   - Junctions: ≥3 ways of a net; a way along a run that only one wire travels doesn't count (point within run box, probe inside).
   - Tags: off upright pins centred on pin column, wired at facing edge; round tags reached at outline outer edge (w/2+sw/2, h/2+sw/2).
   - Lowering (desugar/schematic.rs): declared tags (non-plain shape) get no pose; tied pin = anchor pin with another hop to a stopping device pin; chains whose dest is none or on the same axis turn aside (horizontal pin → D, vertical → R); symbols whose natural attach faces the pin facing (gnd on top, vcc on bottom, nc on left) on tied pins are not upright and travel aside (junction flag false).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

# summarize an SVG from lini: viewBox, nodes at depth (indent based), links
import sys, re, subprocess, os, tempfile

def run(src, args=None, exe='/workspace/executable'):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='summ', dir='/tmp/sch')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# vs2.py BIN_A BIN_B files... : which files pass with A but not B and vice versa (original cached)
import sys, os, subprocess, hashlib
A, B = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sys.argv[3:]
cache = '/tmp/sch/origcache'
os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
def orig(f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    src = open(f, 'rb').read()
    h = hashlib.sha1(src + f.encode()).hexdigest()
    cp = os.path.join(cache, h)
    if os.path.exists(cp + '.out'):
        return open(cp + '.out', 'rb').read(), open(cp + '.err', 'rb').read()
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    open(cp + '.out', 'wb').write(r1.stdout); open(cp + '.err', 'wb').write(r1.stderr)
    return r1.stdout, r1.stderr
def passes(exe, f):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o1, e1 = orig(f)
    try:
        r2 = subprocess.run([exe, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=60)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False
    return o1 == r2.stdout and e1 == r2.stderr
onlyA, onlyB, both = [], [], 0
for f in files:
    a = passes(A, f); b = passes(B, f)
    if a and not b: onlyA.append(os.path.basename(f))
    if b and not a: onlyB.append(os.path.basename(f))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# bridges.py files... : for every bridge we plan, the original's first-part offset and anchor pitch vs ours
import sys, os, subprocess, re
def tops(svg):
    out = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r'<g class="lini-node ([^"]*)" data-id="([^"]*)" transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">', svg):
        out.setdefault(m.group(2), (float(m.group(3)), float(m.group(4))))
    return out
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    env = dict(os.environ, LINI_SCH_DBG='1')
    r = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-sch/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    lines = [l for l in r.stderr.split('\n') if l.startswith('bridge ')]

# bridge cases for fitting the tail rule
cd /tmp/sch
A='|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#X| { side: left; }; |pin#A| { side: right; }; |pin#Y| { side: right; } ]'
B='|component#U2| { cell: 2 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: left; }; |pin#B| { side: left; }; |pin#Q| { side: left; }; |pin#Z| { side: right; } ]'
mkdir -p br
for g in 40 60 80 100 140 200; do
  python3 scripts/mk.py --scope "gap: $g;" br g${g}a "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.B - C2 - |gnd|"
  python3 scripts/mk.py --scope "gap: $g;" br g${g}b "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B"
  python3 scripts/mk.py --scope "gap: $g;" br g${g}c "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|C#C2| \"1u\";;|C#C3| \"1u\";;U1.A - R1 - U2.B;;U2.P - C2 - |gnd|;;U2.Q - C3 - |gnd|"
  python3 scripts/mk.py --scope "gap: $g;" br g${g}d "$A;;$B;;|R#R1| \"10k\";;|R#R2| \"10k\";;U1.A - R1 - R2 - U2.B"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# for failing cases: the differing wire paths (orig / mine), compact
import sys, os, subprocess, re
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    m = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-sch/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    if o == m:
        continue
    wo = re.findall(r'data-from="([^"]+)" data-to="([^"]+)">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', o)
    wm = re.findall(r'data-from="([^"]+)" data-to="([^"]+)">\s*<path d="([^"]+)"', m)
    diffs = [(a, c) for a, c in zip(wo, wm) if a != c]
    if not diffs:
        continue
    print('==', b, len(diffs), 'of', len(wo))
    for a, c in diffs[:2]:
        print('  O', a[0], '->', a[1], a[2])
        print('  M', c[0], '->', c[1], c[2])

#!/bin/bash
# flow fallback: when are wires impossible?
cd /tmp/sch
U='|component#U1| "AMS" [ |pin#SDA| { side: left; }; |pin#SW| { side: right; } ]'
run() {
  python3 scripts/mk.py t10 fp "$1"
  echo "== $2"
  ( cd t10 && /workspace/executable fp.lini 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -v "no placed end" | sed 's/^/   W /' )
  python3 scripts/summ.py -d 2 t10/fp.lini | grep -E "block#|<path" | grep -v "fill=\|linecap" | sed 's/^/   /'
}
run "$U;;|C#C1| \"1u\";;U1.SW - C1 - |gnd|" "right pin, C, gnd"
run "$U;;|C#C1| \"1u\";;U1.SDA - C1 - |gnd|" "left pin, C, gnd"
run "$U;;|C#C1| \"1u\";;U1.SW - C1" "right pin, C"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# region.py FILE x0 y0 x1 y1 : top-level nodes (and their rects) of the original output overlapping a region
import sys, os, subprocess, re
f = sys.argv[1]; x0, y0, x1, y1 = map(float, sys.argv[2:6])
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
# walk with a translate stack
stack = []
for line in o.split('\n'):
    s = line.strip()
    m = re.match(r'<g class="([^"]*)"(?: data-id="([^"]*)")? transform="translate\(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)">', s)
    if m:
        px, py = stack[-1][1] if stack else (0.0, 0.0)
        stack.append((m.group(2) or m.group(1).split()[1] if len(m.group(1).split()) > 1 else m.group(1), (px + float(m.group(3)), py + float(m.group(4)))))
        continue
    if s.startswith('<g'):
        stack.append(('', stack[-1][1] if stack else (0.0, 0.0)))
        continue
    if s == '</g>':
        if stack:
            stack.pop()
        continue
    m = re.match(r'<rect x="([-\d.]+)" y="([-\d.]+)" width="([-\d.]+)" height="([-\d.]+)"', s)
    if m and stack:
        ox, oy = stack[-1][1]
        rx, ry, rw, rh = map(float, m.groups())
        a = (ox + rx, oy + ry, ox + rx + rw, oy + ry + rh)
        if a[0] < x1 and a[2] > x0 and a[1] < y1 and a[3] > y0:
            print('%-30s [%.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f]' % ('/'.join(n for n, _ in stack if n)[-60:], *a))

#!/bin/bash
# a tag on a pin that also has a tie: where does it go?
cd /tmp/sch
B='|component#U2| { cell: 2 1; } [ |pin#S| { side: left; } ]'
run() {
  python3 scripts/mk.py t10 tg "$1"
  echo "== $2"
  ( cd t10 && /workspace/executable tg.lini 2>&1 >/dev/null | sed 's/^/   W /' )
  python3 scripts/summ.py -d 2 t10/tg.lini | grep -E "block#U|label|<path" | sed 's/^/   /'
  python3 scripts/summ.py -m -d 2 t10/tg.lini | grep -E "label" | sed 's/^/   M /'
}
run "|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: right; } ];;$B;;U1.P -> \"TAG\";;U1.P - U2.S" "1 pin"
run "|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: right; }; |pin#Q| { side: right; } ];;$B;;U1.P -> \"TAG\";;U1.P - U2.S" "P of P,Q"
run "|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#Q| { side: right; }; |pin#P| { side: right; } ];;$B;;U1.P -> \"TAG\";;U1.P - U2.S" "P of Q,P"

run "|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: right; } ];;$B;;U1.P - U2.S;;U1.P -> \"TAG\"" "1 pin, tie first"
run "|component#U1| { cell: 1 1; } [ |pin#P| { side: right; } ];;$B;;U1.P - \"NET\";;U1.P - U2.S" "1 pin, net label"
